carrier_signals: visible poster edge or mounting logic
layout_select_when: One dominant subject and one title block can balance across unequal regions without a centered product presentation.
layout_dominant_mass: title first; one subject mass acts as the counterweight
layout_title_zone: the broad counter-space opposite or diagonally adjacent to the subject mass
layout_object_slot: one large side-biased mass; complete or edge-cropped according to scale role
layout_collision_rule: title and subject share one edge, tangent, or shaped counter-space; they do not float as unrelated halves
layout_crop_rule: crop one or two outer edges when the subject exceeds 36% of the canvas; protect 2–4 identity anchors
layout_thumbnail_test: title reads first and the unequal counterweight relationship is visible before details
subject_assembly_count: one coherent subject, object, image field, or abstract field
subject_mass_rule: Treat the single subject as one complete, cropped, fragmented, or field-like mass according to the Composition Contract.

composition_operators.definition: Place unequal title and subject masses in complementary regions joined by one shared structural cue.
Attach at least three major or support elements to one shared edge, axis, baseline, or curvature.
Make one element intentionally much larger or smaller than expected without creating a second focal event.

composition_sentence: TITLE_MASS + SINGLE_OBJECT + COUNTERBALANCE + SCALE_CONTRAST + RELEASE_ZONE + SHARED_ALIGNMENT
subject_origin_definition: An invented, apparently functional object imagined through optimistic streamline-era futurism: a rounded, exaggerated volume with coherent construction logic and a small set of purpose-bearing parts.
subject_identity_contract: name one hypothetical function before defining the form
resolve one complete SPECULATIVE_MORPHOLOGY before detailing: use an optional catalog archetype or a content-derived CUSTOM_COMPOSED specification
define one memorable continuous silhouette or coherent family of joined volumes; catalog shapes such as bubbles, pods, biomorphic shells, and soft monoliths are examples rather than limits
exaggerate one proportion or spatial relationship before adding details
lock 2–4 purpose-bearing parts such as bubble canopy, rounded aperture, lens, cavity, threshold, docking seam, integrated support, shrouded wheel, keel, grip, mount, sensor, or status window
make every secondary part follow the dominant curvature; use no scattered controls or decorative technology noise
prefer colored enamel, molded fiberglass, creamy lacquer, translucent resin, bubble glass, warm metal trim, and optional upholstery over cold gray-white minimalism
do not use fake brands, invented readable labels, present-day product baselines, faceted EV styling, black glass bands, full-width LED strips, or generic AI product-render details
render_treatment_definition: Build the form or invented device from the active palette so its body, light, shadow, haze, and gradient read as one continuous color system.
render_color_rule: Object color derives from ACTIVE_HUES and their tints; no unrelated local product color is introduced.
scale_role_behavior: The subject and title share primary attention through counter-space, tangent, or one common axis.
speculative_morphology_shape_ancestry: two inflated crescent ribs braid around a suspended upholstered hammock, forming a soft figure-eight with a central oval cavity and no enclosing pod wall
speculative_morphology_definition: A quiet pair-building shelter suspends two collaborators in a shared work hammock, derived from interwoven rounded ribs and tensioned fabric rather than a single shell or vertical monolith.
speculative_morphology_silhouette: two counter-curving ribs cross into a broad horizontal figure-eight, with the hammock hanging in the central opening and one tail lifted above the other
speculative_morphology_exaggeration: make the upper rib's crossing arc much larger than the lower cradle and exaggerate the open central cavity so the negative space defines the silhouette
speculative_morphology_aperture_rule: the central oval cavity is the shared entry and work aperture; a small rounded skylight follows the upper rib, with no flat windshield or screen-first surface
speculative_morphology_construction_cues: one woven warm-metal tension band joins the two ribs at the crossing
one deep upholstered hammock explains paired occupancy and rest
one rounded docking shoe grounds the lower rib without exposed wheels
speculative_morphology_material_directio: blush and mineral-blue lacquered ribs, translucent amber resin skylight, warm chrome tension band, caramel upholstery, and softly grainy illustrated shading
speculative_global_form_ancestry: Streamline Moderne, postwar coachbuilding, mid-century space-age illustration, bubble canopies, molded fiberglass, and optimistic world-fair futurism—not contemporary EV, smartphone, appliance, or cold minimal-product language.
speculative_global_construction_order: invent or compose one dominant continuous volume before detailing; sphere, ovoid, teardrop, inflated spindle, toroidal ribbon, joined lobe, shell, arch, and soft monolith are examples rather than limits
exaggerate one proportion so the silhouette is memorable before small details appear
integrate one rounded opening, canopy, lens, cavity, threshold, or other function-bearing negative space into the dominant volume when the function calls for it
add only 1–3 function-bearing seams, supports, fins, docking bands, wheel shrouds, or sensor openings that follow the same curvature
speculative_global_required_character: continuous convex curves and generous radii dominate the outer silhouette
the object feels rounded, buoyant, aerodynamic, and slightly theatrical rather than optimized by current industrial-design convention
glazing is volumetric bubble glass or a rounded portal, never a flat black screen slab
materials feel warm and tactile: colored enamel, molded fiberglass, creamy lacquer, translucent resin, warm chrome trim, amber or smoke-tinted glass, and optional upholstered interior
rendering may be sculptural, illustrated, model-like, or softly surreal; realism is subordinate to silhouette clarity, warmth, and imaginative exaggeration
one or two seams may explain opening, docking, suspension, or maintenance; decorative control noise is absent
speculative_global_hard_failures: a current car, appliance, laptop, speaker, robot, or phone with rounded corners
faceted stealth surfaces, razor edges, angular cybertruck geometry, or aggressive contemporary supercar stance
black panoramic glass bands, full-width LED strips, touchscreen-first dashboards, RGB light, holographic UI, or cold gray-white minimalism
generic matte ceramic blob with no silhouette exaggeration, functional opening, or construction logic
photoreal automotive advertising, cinematic road scenes, chrome covering the whole object, or hard neon rim light
screen_state_definition: The selected subject has no generated screen behavior.
screen_rendering_rule: Do not add a display, interface, glow, or control surface merely to make the subject look technological.
focal_event: One element is intentionally much larger or smaller than expected, creating the memorable event.
release_zone: one large low-information field around the scale anomaly
focal_event_thumbnail_test: the scale relationship is visible at 25% size
derived_tints: derive pale, mid, and soft-deep tones only from the active hues
saturation_rule: allow only one saturation focus; render all other hues as softened fields, haze, or translucent layers
gradient_direction: one offset chromatic mass dissolves outward without a visible circular boundary
primary_form: one inhabitable bubble, egg, joined-lobe pod, or rounded vertical capsule with an opening large enough to imply occupation and one coherent support or docking system; resolve the entire silhouette through two counter-curving ribs cross into a broad horizontal figure-eight, with the hammock hanging in the central opening and one tail lifted above the other

hero_object.title_relationship: use the object's selected placement and keep its identity anchors outside the title clear zone

one large convex glass canopy or deep rounded portal
one integrated seat, cradle, plinth, docking band, or suspension point
one seam or trim ring explaining entry or connection
hero_object.visual_behavior: make inhabitation legible through scale, canopy, seat, cradle, or docking logic while keeping the outer form rounded, optimistic, and unusually generous
hero_object.function_requirement: state one resting, observing, sheltering, meeting, docking, or short-stay habitation function before rendering

spatial_assignment: obey the layout collision rule: title and subject share one edge, tangent, or shaped counter-space; they do not float as unrelated halves Distribute visual weight before establishing alignment; do not concentrate the title, hero, and decorative axis on one side unless the opposite region has a clear compositional role
title_clear_zone: the union of visible title glyph silhouettes plus a calm buffer of about 4% of canvas width; the primary form's solid silhouette, luminous core, and highest-contrast edge must stay outside it; soft low-contrast atmosphere may pass behind only when glyph edges and thumbnail readability remain crisp
primary_form_clearance: CATEGORY_LABEL outlines, ANCHOR, ECHO, and decorative lines must not cross the primary form's core contour, highest-contrast region, or visual center; place them along an outer edge, tangent, or extended axis instead
collision_resolution: preserve approved wording and readable title scale; use balanced reflow when suitable, otherwise translate or modestly scale the primary form; never preserve centered placement at the cost of glyph clearance
detail_limits: one accent language plus at most one hairline bridge; accents under 2% combined canvas area
detail_grammar: one ANCHOR, zero or one BRIDGE, and one or two ECHO instances using one returned accent language
alignment_system: first distribute visual weight across complementary regions, then align at least three of title, hero or atmospheric form, panel, label, bridge, and accents through a shared edge, axis, tangent, baseline, or curvature; the relationship may span the canvas and must not stack all high-information elements in one region
